summary.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 82% YoY to INR136.5 crore and PAT 66.9% to INR17.6 crore, helped by INR28 crore of trading sales.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was INR136.5 crore against INR75 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR26.4 crore (up 49.2% YoY) and PAT of INR17.6 crore (up 66.9%). Management attributed part of the sequential revenue mix to trading sales, which fell from about INR46 crore in Q1 to INR28 crore in Q2 while manufacturing revenue rose from INR99.57 crore to INR108.62 crore. Freight costs on long-distance exports rose 3x to 5x, lifting other expenses to INR20.87 crore from INR18.57 crore, which management said was more than recovered from customers. The company announced a INR75-85 crore Dahej expansion and a smaller CoatIcon pharma tablet-coating capex of INR25-35 crore, both with construction starting in Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Manufacturing (food colours and specialty dyes)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 manufacturing revenue was INR108.62 crore, up from INR99.57 crore in Q1, on 1,554 metric tons of sales. H1 manufacturing sales were stated as INR208 crore, up about 42% from INR146 crore.

segments.name: Trading (raw materials and petrochemical derivatives)
segments.commentary: Trading sales were INR75 crore in H1 FY27 against about INR16 crore a year earlier, driven by spot opportunities and hedging of raw material supply. Management said it is low-margin (3-4%) and not part of core strategy.

segments.name: CoatIcon (pharma tablet coatings)
segments.commentary: Launched less than a year ago; current sales are small samples of about INR8-15 lakh per month to smaller pharma companies. Management said Colorcon holds about 90% of the market.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 expected to look very similar to or slightly better than H1, based on current order position.
Full capacity utilisation at Dahej targeted during FY27.
Effluent treatment plant changes expected to add 50-75 tons per month at Dahej; around 7,000 tons per year achievable, with output starting from Q4 FY27 (analyst cited about 1,875 tons per quarter).
Dahej expansion: INR75-85 crore capex, construction from last quarter of FY27, commissioning mid-to-end FY28, expected revenue INR225-250 crore.
CoatIcon on-ground activities to start in 2-3 months with INR25-35 crore investment; both projects to run concurrently.
Expansion to be funded mainly by internal accruals (company earning over INR20 crore per quarter), with a possible small term loan.
risks_watch: Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption: higher freight, insurance and energy costs, plus working capital pressure.
Trading revenue volatility: INR46 crore in Q1 fell to INR28 crore in Q2, so headline growth quality depends on trading.
Working capital outflow of INR14.7 crore in H1 FY27 versus a INR13.8 crore inflow last year.
CoatIcon approvals may take 2-3 years and the market is about 90% controlled by Colorcon.
Dahej capacity uplift from effluent treatment plant changes is due from Q4 FY27; execution risk on capex timing.
Investor communication: the deck was uploaded shortly before the call and plant visit requests remain pending.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, pipeline and H2 outlook, while acknowledging a geopolitically difficult environment. Management was evasive on CoatIcon revenue, and on capex it gave only ranges and no net cash figure. Tone turned defensive when investors raised share-price performance and call timing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trading sales rise nearly 5x to INR75 crore in H1 when manufacturing rose 42% to INR208 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said trading is driven by spot opportunities and excess raw material positions taken to secure supply amid Middle East disruption; margins are 3-4%, and surplus funds meant for capex are being used in the interim.

capex_capacity: Dahej expansion: INR75-85 crore capex on a new plot in Dahej GIDC (16,834 sq m, recently allotted); construction to begin in last quarter of FY27; commissioning targeted mid-to-end FY28; expected revenue INR225-250 crore; structural and process flow drawings still being confirmed; project described as confidential in detail; capex phased over about 1.5 years.

CoatIcon: dedicated manufacturing facility being set up at Roha on plot owned by wholly owned subsidiary Arjun; on-ground activities to start in 2-3 months with INR25-35 crore investment; runs concurrently with Dahej project.

Installed capacity presented as 7,500 MT (earlier 3,900 + 4,200 = 8,100 MT); management said the plant's yearly potential remains 8,100 tons, with the 7,500 MT figure reflecting portfolio mix and smaller batch sizes for high-water-volume items; 7,500 MT equals about 90% utilisation.
Dahej effluent treatment plant changes expected to add 50-75 tons per month; around 7,000 tons per year achievable, starting Q4 FY27 (analyst equated this to about 1,875 tons per quarter).
Pilot plant set up for new specialty product line; pilot production and sampling to potential customers has started; full-scale capex planned at Dahej.

Full capacity utilisation at Dahej targeted during FY27; expansion to be funded mainly by internal accruals (company earning over INR20 crore per quarter), with a possible small term loan for working capital comfort.

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 similar to or slightly better than H1 (H1 revenue INR282.8 cr), with full Dahej utilisation targeted in FY27 and ETP changes adding ~7,000 t/yr from Q4; the INR75-85 cr Dahej expansion (commissioning mid-to-end FY28) is backed by a plot allotment but few concrete orders, so support is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: PAT margin slipped to 12.9% from 14.1% as freight costs rose 3x-5x and other expenses reached INR20.87 crore from INR18.57 crore, with low-margin trading (3-4%) diluting mix as it fell from INR46 crore to INR28 crore.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation is about 90% (7,500 MT on 8,100 MT potential), ETP changes add 50-75 t/month (~7,000 t/yr) from Q4 FY27, and the INR75-85 crore Dahej expansion commissions mid-to-end FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides H2 FY27 similar to or slightly better than H1 (H1 revenue INR282.8 crore), manufacturing volume rose to 1,554 MT in Q2, and full Dahej utilisation is targeted during FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Dahej INR75-85 crore and CoatIcon INR25-35 crore are already announced with construction starting in Q4 FY27, and utilisation of about 90% supports further capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is held at H2 similar to or slightly better than H1, with no explicit raise, and trading revenue has fallen from INR46 crore to INR28 crore quarter on quarter.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Middle East and Strait of Hormuz disruption is lifting freight and energy costs, working capital outflow was INR14.7 crore in H1 versus a INR13.8 crore inflow last year, and Dahej capex execution timing carries risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A pilot plant for a new specialty product line has started sampling to customers, with full-scale capex planned at Dahej, but no launch date is given; CoatIcon sales are only INR8-15 lakh per month.

rows.label: CoatIcon pharma tablet coatings at Roha
rows.why: On-ground work starts in 2-3 months with INR25-35 crore investment, but approvals may take 2-3 years and Colorcon holds about 90% of the market; current sales are only INR8-15 lakh per month.

rows.label: Working capital outflow in H1 FY27
rows.why: H1 FY27 outflow was INR14.7 crore against a INR13.8 crore inflow last year, and trading inventory positions tie up cash, though surplus funds are being used for interim needs.

rows.label: Expansion funded by internal accruals
rows.why: The company earns over INR20 crore per quarter (Q2 PAT INR17.6 crore), so the INR75-85 crore Dahej and INR25-35 crore CoatIcon capex is mainly internally funded, with a possible small term loan.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 outlook, Dahej utilisation and the expansion pipeline, but was evasive on CoatIcon revenue and gave only capex ranges; analysts pressed on trading-driven growth quality, share price and call timing.
